questions.prompt: `Main` starts 5 threads that each run `Increment` and then joins them all before printing `Counter = {counter}`. What is printed?
options: A value that changes from run to run, usually below 500000
`Counter = 100000`
`Counter = 500000`
Nothing, because the threads deadlock on `sync`
questions.explanation: Every `counter++` runs inside `lock (sync)`, so only one thread updates it at a time and no increments are lost: 5 × 100,000 = 500,000.

questions.prompt: Async code must limit itself to 2 concurrent HTTP calls without blocking threads while it waits. Which primitive fits?
options: `lock`, because it is the lightest option
`SemaphoreSlim`, using `WaitAsync`
A named `Mutex`, using `WaitOne`
`Monitor.TryEnter` with a timeout
questions.explanation: `SemaphoreSlim` is a lightweight in-process semaphore that supports `WaitAsync` for async throttling; `lock` cannot be awaited and blocks the thread.

questions.prompt: You want a second copy of your app to detect that another instance is already running. Which primitive does the lesson use for this?
options: `lock` on a `static readonly object`
`SemaphoreSlim(1)`
`Monitor.Pulse`
A named `Mutex`, checking `createdNew`
questions.explanation: A `Mutex` can be named to synchronize across processes. In the single-instance demo the first run gets `createdNew = true`; a second run while the first holds it gets `false` and exits. `lock` is single-process only.

questions.prompt: In the producer/consumer example, Thread A calls `Monitor.Wait(sync)` inside `lock (sync)`. What does that call do?
options: Releases the lock and waits until it is signaled
Keeps holding the lock and spins until the condition is true
Throws, because you can't wait while holding a lock
Wakes every other thread waiting on `sync`
questions.explanation: `Monitor.Wait` releases the lock and waits; Thread B can then take the lock, set the condition and call `Monitor.Pulse(sync)` to wake one waiter.

questions.prompt: A `SemaphoreSlim` allows 2 concurrent tasks. Both are inside, each awaiting an async call and then updating the same shared value. Can they interfere with each other?
options: No, `SemaphoreSlim` makes the protected section atomic
No, because `WaitAsync` runs the two tasks one after another
Yes, because it only limits how many can enter, not what those inside do to shared data
Only if the semaphore was created with a name
questions.explanation: With a concurrency of 2, two tasks may be inside at the same time, so they can affect each other. `SemaphoreSlim` limits how many enter; it doesn't prevent interference between those allowed in.

questions.prompt: A process holding a named `Mutex` is killed without releasing it. What does a second process waiting on that mutex get?
options: It waits forever, because the mutex is never released
It acquires the mutex and receives an `AbandonedMutexException`
`OpenExisting` returns a brand-new unowned mutex
Its `WaitOne()` returns `false` and it must retry
questions.explanation: If a mutex is abandoned (its owner terminated without releasing), waiters get `AbandonedMutexException`; the lesson's demo shows the second copy acquiring the mutex and immediately receiving it.
